name: Campinasuchus
sum: Campinasuchus is an extinct baurusuchid crocodyliform from the Late Cretaceous of Minas Gerais, Brazil, with a deep, laterally compressed skull and blade-like teeth.
wsnote: No body-length estimate is given in the sources consulted.
holotype: CPP 1235, a well-preserved posterior skull and partial rostrum (Três Antas Farm, Campina Verde, Minas Gerais; Adamantina Formation, Bauru Basin).
material: Four partial skulls (CPP 1234-1237); the postcranial skeleton was described in a later study.
biology: A small pit on the premaxilla received the first lower tooth when the jaws closed; the skull was deep and laterally compressed with large blade-like teeth.
author: Carvalho et al. 2011
